interpretation: Instruction (from ep.observe()): 'Pick up the red cube and gently stack it on top of the green cube, then release it.' Robot: capx_robosuite_panda, one 7-DoF arm, parallel-jaw gripper (stroke 0.08 m, max_width 0.079 m, closed_empty 0.985, held_below 0.95, closing axis x, approach axis z), one scene camera (robot0_robotview, at x=1.0 m facing the robot, 45 deg down), no wrist camera. Perception found two objects: obj1 'green 7x7x4 cm' (the green cube) and obj2 labelled 'brown 5x5x3 cm', which is clearly the red cube in the RGB image (mean colour 138,46,55). Its aabb labels were inflated, so I measured both from top-face points: the green cube is about 5 cm (top-face OBB 4.95 x 4.93 cm, top z -0.0627, centre (0.496, -0.025), yaw 47.4/-42.6 deg) and the red cube about 4 cm (3.96 x 3.94 cm, top z -0.0727, centre (0.601, -0.016), yaw 28.9 deg). The table is at z about -0.111. Goal state: the red cube resting upright on the green cube's top face, released (gripper open, not held), placed gently (lowered to a few mm above contact rather than dropped), with the green cube undisturbed. Nothing was ambiguous apart from the red/brown colour label.
plan: Top-down grasp of the red cube with the closing axis along one of its face normals, then lower it onto the green cube with its faces aligned to the green cube's, release from about 2-4 mm above contact, retreat straight up, and verify. Grasp yaw: -61.1 deg was chosen over the 180-degree-equivalent 118.9 deg because IK for 118.9 put joint 7 within 0.13 rad of its limit at the grasp and within 0.018 rad at the matching place yaw, while -61.1 / -42.6 left more than 0.7 rad of margin. The place yaw of -42.6 deg is the green cube's face yaw closest to the grasp yaw (an 18.5 deg turn in transit). Grasp TCP height -0.087 (about 2.4 cm above the table) puts the pads around the middle of the 4 cm cube and keeps the fingertips above the cube's bottom edge, so they cannot touch the green top when placing. Place height came from re-measuring the held cube's top in the cloud after the lift: TCP_place = -0.0777 + h_red + clearance. The top-face depth bias cancels between the two cubes; with h_red between 3.86 and 4.0 cm I chose -0.0355, a 2-4 mm gap. The plan changed in two places: the approach had to be lengthened from 3.0 s to 4.5 s (velocity limit from the large wrist rotation), and an explicit gripper open was added because the gripper had only reached 0.471 at the end of the approach.

steps.what: Read the embodiment, instruction, budget; showed robotview RGB, annotated ids, 3D views; measured both cubes' top faces and the table height from object_points/cloud.
steps.why: Identify the red and green cubes, their true size, pose and yaw before moving.
steps.result: Red = obj2 (mislabelled brown, 4 cm, yaw 28.9), green = obj1 (5 cm, yaw 47.4), table z -0.111. Step 0.

steps.what: Inspected collision spheres (ep.robot()) relative to the TCP.
steps.why: No tip_reach_m given; needed to know how far the fingers reach below the TCP.
steps.result: Finger sphere envelope reaches 2.2 cm below the TCP and spans the fingers' full travel (x 0 to +/-6.3 cm) regardless of the real opening, so check_batch finger contacts with the target cube are artefacts of the envelope.

steps.what: IK for grasp/place at both 180-degree-equivalent yaws.
steps.why: Pick the wrist orientation with joint-limit margin.
steps.result: Chose grasp yaw -61.1 (q7 about -0.21) and place yaw -42.6 (q7 about -0.63); 118.9/137.4 were near the joint-7 limit.

steps.what: Approach: top-down to 4.5 cm above the red cube (TCP z -0.02) with gripper command open, 4.5 s.
steps.why: Get over the red cube with the fingers aligned to its faces.
steps.result: The 3.0 s version was refused as too fast (min 3.42 s); 4.5 s executed fine (96 steps). Gripper read only 0.471 (gap 4.2 cm) at the end, too narrow for a 4 cm cube. Step 96.

steps.why: Fully open before descending over the 4 cm cube.

steps.what: Descend to grasp height TCP z -0.087, 2.0 s; image before closing.
steps.why: Put the pads around the middle of the cube with the fingertips clear of the table.
steps.result: Image 007 shows the red cube centred between the open fingers with clearance on both sides. Step 162.

steps.what: Close gripper (1 s), then lift to TCP z 0.0 (2 s).
steps.why: Grasp, and clear the green cube's top by about 4 cm for the transfer.
steps.result: Closed reading 0.507 (gap 3.94 cm), consistent with the 4 cm cube held; 0.504 after the lift. The green cube was hidden behind the hand (objects() empty), not moved. Step 228.

steps.what: Measured the held cube's red points in the cloud.
steps.why: Detect slip and set the place height from measurement.
steps.result: Red top at TCP +1.55 cm, bottom edge at about TCP -2.1 to -2.3 cm, matching the grasp (no meaningful slip).

steps.what: Transfer above the green centre (0.4962, -0.025, z 0.0) while turning to yaw -42.6, 2.5 s; imaged and re-measured.
steps.why: Align the red cube over the green cube with matching face orientation.
steps.result: Image 010 shows red above green with a gap. Green points unchanged (x max 0.5306, top about -0.061). Red top still at TCP +1.5 cm. Step 284.

steps.what: Slow descent to TCP z -0.0355, 2.5 s; imaged while still holding.
steps.why: Bring the red cube's bottom to 2-4 mm above the green top for a gentle release.
steps.result: Image 012: red sitting right on the green top, centred and aligned; red top at z -0.0205 (TCP +1.5 cm, no slip). Gripper still 0.503. Step 340.

steps.why: Release the cube onto the green cube.
steps.result: Gripper 0.024 (gap 7.81 cm). Red top dropped about 1.3 mm to z -0.022, so the red cube now rests on the green. Image 014. Step 360.

steps.what: Retreat straight up 10 cm (2 s, xy drift 0.04 mm in preview), then move to (0.40, 0.12, 0.12) (2.5 s).
steps.why: Leave without touching the stack and clear the camera's view for verification.

steps.what: Final verification from the real camera plus rendered closeup/3D views; quantitative top-face fit.
steps.why: Check each part of the instruction before finishing.
steps.result: Red top-face centre (0.4967, -0.0252), 0.5 mm from the green centre (0.4962, -0.025); slope 0.06 deg (level); yaw -42.6 (aligned with green); red top z -0.022, so its bottom is at about -0.061, which is the green top; gripper open (0.0); green cube's visible extent unchanged. Called finish_episode at step 462 of 1500, wall about 8 min.

key_images.caption: Start: green 5 cm cube (back) and red 4 cm cube (front) on the table, robotview camera.
Perceived ids: obj1 green, obj2 (labelled brown) = red cube.
At grasp height: red cube centred between the fully open fingers, before closing.
Red cube grasped (reading 0.507) and lifted; green cube hidden behind the hand.
Red cube carried over the green cube, faces aligned, about 4 cm gap.
Red cube lowered to just above or on the green top, still held.
After opening: red cube resting on the green, fingers clear on both sides.
Final state, arm parked away: red cube stacked on the green cube.
Final close crop: red upright, centred and aligned on green.
Closeup renders from 4 azimuths plus real crop confirming the stack.

lessons: Perception's colour label can be wrong ('brown' for a clearly red cube) and aabb sizes are inflated for rotated objects; fit an OBB to the top-face points (z within a few mm of the max) to get true size, centre and yaw.

A gripper open command attached to a motion waypoint may not finish opening by the end of the motion (it read 0.471 here); check gripper_measured and issue an explicit gripper(False) before descending around an object.

On this embodiment the check's finger spheres cover the fingers' whole travel regardless of the actual opening, so finger contacts with the object being grasped are expected; judge clearance geometrically from gripper_gap_m and the object width instead.
Choose between 180-degree-equivalent top-down yaws by IK joint-limit margin for both the grasp and the place pose, not just the smallest rotation; large wrist rotations need more time (min_duration).

Compute the place height from the held object's measured top relative to the TCP and the target's measured top, using the same top-face measurement for both so depth bias cancels; a 2-4 mm release gap gives a gentle, stable stack.
With a single front scene camera the hand hides the target during transport; it becomes visible again close to the place pose, and moving the arm aside afterwards gives an unobstructed final check.
